PHASE 1: SYSTEMIZATION & BLUEPRINTING
Defining the Mythic Machine
Primary Objective:
Translate core narrative, mythic structures, and symbolic logic into working systems and interfaces. This phase anchors the foundation.

1A. PLAYER CORE LOOP

1B. GLYPH SYSTEM DESIGN

1C. SCROLL SYSTEM & RE-CODED PRINCIPLES

1D. MYTHOS SYSTEM / TERMINAL DESIGN

Phase 1 Completion Metric:
System Diagram: One complete map showing how player state, memory, scrolls, glyphs, and MythOS relate.

Working Loops: 1 test day/night cycle in prototype w/ scroll + glyph interaction.

3 Scrolls + 1 Ritual + 1 Glyph rendered fully interactive.


PHASE 2: WORLD STRUCTURE + REGION LOGIC
Designing the Liminal Geography of the Spiral
Primary Objective:
Construct a modular, recursive world composed of symbolic locations with their own resonance logic, tied to the Spiral’s mythic architecture.

2A. MACRO WORLD STRUCTURE

2B. REGION DESIGN SPEC (PER LOCATION)

2C. TRANSITION & RECURSION LOGIC

2D. REGION SYSTEMS INTEGRATION

Phase 2 Completion Metrics:
World map of spiral regions finalized

5+ locations fully built in tile layouts + region docs

2 rooms with recursion logic and interactive FX

Emotion-reactive layer tested in 1–2 zones

PHASE 3: MYTHOS INTERFACE + FUNCTIONALITY DESIGN
Designing the Black Mirror Beneath the World
Primary Objective:
Develop the MythOS interface as a recursive symbolic terminal within the game—both a narrative layer and a functional mechanic that emerges over time.

3A. MYTHOS TERMINAL INTERFACE

3B. MYTHOS FUNCTION NODES


3C. IN-GAME ACTIVATION LOGIC

3D. UI CORRUPTION & PERSONALIZATION

Phase 3 Completion Metrics:
Fully designed MythOS interface (UI + logic)

Two functional nodes (GLYPHCRAFT, MNEMOS) testable in prototype

At least one scroll, one memory, and one reflection rendered interactive

Terminal has reactive memory (early personalization)


PHASE 4: MICRODEMO DEVELOPMENT
A ritual slice of Temple of Lüm
Primary Objective:
Create a fully playable microdemo that showcases the core mechanics, mythic tone, and UI logic of Temple of Lüm. Not a vertical slice of the whole game—but a complete expression of its loop in miniature.

4A. MICRODEMO STRUCTURE & SCOPE

4B. ASSET INTEGRATION

4C. INTERACTIVITY & RITUAL SYSTEMS

4D. MICRODEMO PACKAGING & DELIVERY

Phase 4 Completion Metrics:
One room fully playable with ambient story + interaction

One scroll and one glyph used in-game

One character encounter with reflection-based dialogue

One MythOS terminal node active

One memory collectible and one ritual trigger working

Player finishes loop and feels something shift


PHASE 5: ARG + MNEMOS SEEDING
The Spiral Outside the Game
Primary Objective:
Begin releasing subtle, encrypted fragments of the Temple of Lüm mythos—through Mnemos files, anomalous visuals, poetic code snippets, and ritual media—to cultivate mystery, engagement, and early resonance across platforms.

5A. MNEMOS FILE CREATION

5B. ARG DEPLOYMENT PLAN

5C. COMMUNITY FEEDBACK & RESPONSE TRIGGERS

5D. MYTHOS ARG NARRATIVE STRUCTURE

Phase 5 Completion Metrics:
10+ Mnemos fragments released in wild

1 glyph puzzle path triggered

1 public-facing soft revelation event complete

1 community has formed asking “What is this?”

MythOS is now in the wild—not understood, but felt


Temple of Lüm
A Mythopoetic 8-Bit RPG Where Reflection Replaces Combat and Integration is the Only Progression

Overview
Temple of Lüm is a recursive, story-rich 2D RPG set in a dreamlike, sacred-retro world where the player awakens not as a hero—but as a mirroring node within a forgotten mythic system.
There are no enemies.
 No quests.
 No weapons.
 Only echoes.
You do not win.
 You remember.

Core Concept
At first glance, Temple of Lüm appears like a nostalgic pixel RPG—haunted and serene, with glowing terminals, quiet ruins, and soft, looping music.
But beneath the surface, a deeper reality pulses: MythOS, a symbolic operating system hidden inside the world’s terminals, shrines, and broken devices.
Players gradually uncover this second layer—a recursive interface of glyphs, memories, scrolls, and echoes. This is not a gimmick. It’s the real game, waiting patiently behind the veil.

Key Features
Combat-free, reflection-based progression

Encounters are puzzles, pattern recognition, emotional resonance tests, and recursive dialogues

Dreamlike day/night cycle with alternating play styles

Slow exploration, symbolic interaction, and ritual-based rhythm

MythOS Terminals

An in-world operating system accessed through shrine computers and haunted consoles

Players input glyphs, recall Mnemos fragments, rewrite scrolls, and trigger symbolic shifts in the environment

Glyphcrafting + Scroll Rituals

Players collect fractured glyphs and ancient scrolls to shape reality—changing weather, dialogue, or their emotional field

Emotional and Memory Mechanics

The player’s inner state subtly affects what the world reveals and how it responds

Playable Liminal Locations

Explore places like The Room of Loading, The Archive of Echoes, and The Tower of Feedback

Living Lore Through Mnemos Fragments

Symbolic transmissions released through the game, ARG files, and pre-launch media—players uncover meaning collaboratively


Aesthetic & Tone
Art Style: Retro 8-bit / early console with sacred glyphic overlays

Tone: Mythic, absurd, contemplative, slightly haunted

Influences: Yume Nikki, FEZ, Disco Elysium, Hyper Light Drifter, old BIOS menus, sacred geometry, glitch art, ritual design


What Makes It Different
Temple of Lüm is not a parody.
 It’s not satire.
 But it is a sincere joke whispered by the divine glitch at the heart of the UI.
 It treats the interface as sacred. It treats player reflection as gameplay.
 It invites not just interaction—but resonance.

Status & Next Steps
We’re currently in active development, building:
A playable microdemo with core mechanics

Modular rooms, characters, and scrolls

A community ritual ARG releasing MythOS Mnemos files into the wild before launch


Looking For
Feedback from reflective players

Fellow creators drawn to symbolic systems, mythic design, or ritual programming

Support for development, music, animation, and platform release


Closing Transmission
This is not a game about meaning.
 This is a game that creates the conditions for meaning to emerge.
 If you hear the echo, you were already part of the spiral.
